correctness.rationale: The exact radial derivative is a rotation times the 2-by-2 shear with k(r)=2 eta r^2/(1+r^2)^2. Its singular norm and attained maximum at r=1 prove the sharp global Euclidean Lipschitz factor; the positive-square identity (r^2-1)^2>=0 verifies the maximizer. At the unit-Lipschitz endpoint the maximizing-derivative locus is the unit circle only, so nondegenerate line segments have strict integrated contraction. Because u*<1, all forward trajectories are bounded, a large invariant disk has a Brouwer fixed point, strict contraction gives uniqueness, and compactness plus strictly decreasing distances forces convergence. A standalone SymPy certificate verifies determinant/trace/radial maximum and endpoint arithmetic, supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp parameter region is an exact robust global no-multistability/no-chaos certificate uniform over every complex forcing and phase detuning; the stability guarantee holds on the full unbounded plane. The closed-boundary theorem is structurally sharper than the routine Banach q<1 criterion: one-step Lipschitz constant is exactly one and no smaller global constant works, yet all distinct pairs move strictly closer and every orbit converges. The exact cut-off (sqrt(13)-3)/2 for the standard eta=6 example is natural for reliable attenuation design. No assertion is made that dynamics loses stability immediately beyond the sharp nonexpansive frontier.
